{{short description|Finnish academic (born 1941)}}
[[File:Pekka-Pyykko-1991.jpg|thumb|right|Pekka Pyykkö in 1991]]
'''Veli Pekka Pyykkö''' (born 12 October 1941)<ref name="curriculum">{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.helsinki.fi/~pyykko/curriculum/curriculum.html|title=Curriculum vitae|work=chem.helsinki.fi|date=2012-04-25|accessdate=2012-05-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219013538/http://www.chem.helsinki.fi/~pyykko/curriculum/curriculum.html|archive-date=2012-02-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a Finnish academic. He was professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref name="curriculum"/> From 2009&ndash;2012, he was the chairman of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]]. He is known for his extension to the [[periodic table]] of elements,<ref name="nyt">{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Siobhan |title=Is It Time to Upend the Periodic Table? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/27/science/periodic-table-elements-chemistry.html |accessdate=7 December 2019 |work=The New York Times |date=27 August 2019}}</ref><ref name="science">{{cite news |last1=Kean |first1=Sam |title=A storied Russian lab is trying to push the periodic table past its limits—and uncover exotic new elements |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/storied-russian-lab-trying-push-periodic-table-past-its-limits-and-uncover-exotic-new |accessdate=7 December 2019 |publisher=Science |date=30 January 2019}}</ref> known as the [[Pyykkö model]].<ref name="atsumi">{{cite journal |last1=Atsumi |first1=Michiko |title=SCCJ Cafe -Season 3-Theoretical Chemistry in Nordic (2)"The Extended Periodic Table − Pyykkö Model" |journal=Journal of Computer Chemistry, Japan |date=2013 |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=A18–A20 |doi=10.2477/jccj.2013-0008 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Pyykkö has also studied the [[Relativistic quantum chemistry|relativistic effects]] present in heavy atoms and their effects in [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|NMR]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vaara |first1=Juha |last2=Pyykkö |first2=Pekka |date=2003-02-15 |title=Relativistic, nearly basis-set-limit nuclear magnetic shielding constants of the rare gases He–Rn: A way to absolute nuclear magnetic resonance shielding scales |url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1545718 |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=118 |issue=7 |pages=2973–2976 |doi=10.1063/1.1545718 |issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Pyykkö model==
{{main|Pyykkö model}}
After the 118 elements now known, Pekka Pyykkö predicts that the orbital shells will fill up in this order:
*8s,
*5g,
*the first two spaces of 8p,
*6f,
*7d,
*9s,
*the first two spaces of 9p,
*the rest of 8p.<ref name="pyykko"/>
He also suggests that period 8 be split into three parts:
*8a, containing 8s,
*8b, containing the first two elements of 8p,
*8c, containing 7d and the rest of 8p.<ref name="pyykko">{{Cite journal |last1=Pyykkö |first1=Pekka |title=A suggested periodic table up to Z≤ 172, based on Dirac–Fock calculations on atoms and ions |journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=161–8 |year=2011 |pmid=20967377 |doi=10.1039/c0cp01575j |bibcode = 2011PCCP...13..161P |s2cid=31590563 }}</ref>

The compact version:<ref name="pyykko" /><br>
[[File:Pyykko periodic table 172.svg|800px|center|Extended periodic table. P. Pyykkö, PCCP 2011, 13, 161. @RSC. Reprinted with permission.]]

Pekka Pyykkö correctly predicted the existence of [[chemical bond]]s between [[gold]] and the [[noble gas]] [[xenon]], which is usually inert; this bond is known to occur in the [[cation]]ic [[complex (chemistry)|complex]] [[tetraxenonogold(II)]] ({{chem|AuXe|4|2+}}). He also correctly predicted the existence of gold–[[carbon]] [[triple bond]]s.<ref>Scientific American June 2013, "Cracks in the Periodic Table". p. 72.</ref>
